title: ‘We’ve been taking our time’: Buzzy AI biotech Xaira reveals antibody platform, first taste of pipeline
summary: When Xaira Therapeutics first debuted in 2024 with a gobsmacking $1 billion in funding, a natural expectation would have been for a flurry of further activity to follow. Instead, the buzzy AI biotech went quiet.

title: Chutes & Ladders—Bayer taps new chief medical officer; Cantor appointed PhRMA CEO
summary: Eric Cantor, who represented Virginia in the U.S. House of Representatives for 14 years and served as House majority leader from 2011 to 2014, will step up as PhRMA’s next president and CEO on Nov. 9. Plus, Bayer has a new chief medical officer.

title: Novartis pens $7.8B deal for Abogen's in vivo autoimmune T-cell engager
summary: Novartis is paying Abogen Biosciences $575 million upfront for an mRNA-encoded T-cell engager that showed early clinical promise in autoimmune disease. The deal, which includes up to $7.2 billion in milestones, comes weeks after Novartis paused an autoimmune CAR-T program over three deaths.

title: Immunotherapy startup Adecto blames ‘risk-averse funding environment’ for closing down
summary: Adecto Pharmaceuticals’ 12-year story has come to an end as the immunotherapy biotech blamed a “risk-averse funding environment” for shutting up shop.

title: Abbott launches SimpleScreen CRC blood test in the US
summary: Abbott is kick-starting the U.S. commercial launch of SimpleScreen CRC, an FDA-approved blood-based colorectal cancer (CRC) screening test for adults age 45 and older who are at average risk for the disease.

title: Patient death in BMS pulmonary fibrosis trial raises questions, but analysts unshaken
summary: The revelation of a patient death in Bristol Myers Squibb’s phase 3 trial of a potential pulmonary fibrosis treatment has raised concerns ahead of the study’s readout, but analysts were quick to dispel worries about broader implications for the drug mechanism involved.

title: Roche launches simultaneous screening test for SMA, SCID and SCD
summary: Roche Diagnostics has launched a new in vitro diagnostic test for newborn screening to detect a series of rare disorders.

title: Biopharma recruiters see ‘signs of recovery’ as layoffs remain cool in Q3’26
summary: A more subdued volume of biopharma layoffs continued into the third quarter of 2026, validating predictions that the sector has moved beyond the avalanche of redundancies experienced last year.

title: Foghorn lays off 40% of employees as Lilly cancer collab collapses over poor data

title: ‘We’re so close to the tech companies’: Genentech CEO talks Fierce through vision for the future

title: Zealand's stock slides as Boehringer-partnered obesity drug underwhelms again in phase 3

title: Sanofi pays Dupixent partner Regeneron $1B upfront for 4 early-stage assets to ignite R&D

title: In conversation with Sergey Stavisky
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02443-5As part of our special issue on Neurotechnology, we spoke with Sergey Stavisky, Associate Professor at the University of California, Davis, about the breakthroughs that have transformed speech neuroprostheses from proof-of-concept demonstrations into practical communication systems. He reflects on the scientific surprises, engineering challenges and ethical questions that are shaping the future of neural interfaces.

title: In conversation with Miguel Nicolelis
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02467-xAs part of our special issue on neurotechnology, we spoke with Miguel Nicolelis, Professor Emeritus at Duke University and founder of the Edmond and Lily Safra International Neuroscience Institute, about the bold ideas that have defined his career, from helping to pioneer brain–machine interfaces to establishing a neuroscience institute in northeastern Brazil with the goal of driving social transformation. He considers the scientific discoveries, technological hurdles and ethical questions that continue to shape the future of neural interfaces and neurorehabilitation.

title: In conversation with Richard Andersen
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02450-6As part of our special issue on neurotechnology, we spoke with Richard Andersen, James G. Boswell Professor of Neuroscience at Caltech, about the discoveries that helped to establish the posterior parietal cortex as a key hub for intention and action planning. He looks back on decades of discoveries in the posterior parietal cortex and discusses how advances in neural recording, decoding and computation are reshaping our understanding of cognition.

title: In conversation with Edward Chang
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02453-3As part of our special issue on neurotechnology, we spoke with Edward Chang, Margaret Liu Collins and Edward B. Collins distinguished Professor and Chair of neurosurgery at the University of California, San Francisco, about the evolution of speech brain–computer interfaces (BCIs). He discusses how advances in AI are accelerating the translation of BCIs into the clinic, the challenge of restoring natural communication, and why large-scale neural datasets may ultimately help build computational models of the human brain.
